rounds.text: Supra Trends Ltd trades at an accessible market capitalisation of ₹ 34.5 Cr [E2] and a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.42x based on a book value of ₹ 10.3 against a share price of ₹ 14.6 [E1]. Operational comparisons against the broader industry reveal relative resilience, as the company's return on assets of -6.41% [E7] and return on equity of -9.94% [E8] both significantly outperform brutal sector benchmarks of -104.68% [E7] and -11.79% [E8] respectively. Furthermore, recent operational momentum is showing tangible signs of life through quarter-over-quarter sales expansion [E48], which is reinforced by analytical signals indicating that profit growth recently exceeds one-year price growth by 31%, pointing to early stages of outperforming expectations [E41]. This emerging fundamental improvement occurs within a healthy macroeconomic backdrop defined by robust sector tailwinds, including a sector median sales growth of 14.1% [E58] and a sector median profit growth of 20.6% [E57]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E3], the stock rests at a depressed 9 percent of its 52-week range [E4], and compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted sharply by -267% [E14].

Conceded: return on assets of -6.41% [E7] and return on equity of -9.94% [E8] technically outperform the deeply negative sector benchmarks. However, the bull frames these metrics as strengths while ignoring that they still represent value-destroying, negative underlying profitability [E7, E8]. The claimed operational momentum from quarter-over-quarter sales expansion [E48] is completely overwhelmed by catastrophic trailing twelve-month compounded sales contraction of -267% [E14] and a -42% drop in compounded profit growth [E15]. The assertion of early outperformance via profit growth exceeding one-year price growth [E41] offers little comfort when the stock is pinned near the absolute bottom at 9% of its 52-week range [E4] and pays a complete zero dividend yield [E3]. Finally, pointing to robust sector tailwinds of 14.1% sales growth [E58] and 20.6% profit growth [E57] only highlights Supra Trends' severe underperformance against its peers, given its own miserable 2% 10-year compounded sales growth [E13] and negative earnings trajectory [E52].
